Outcome: Depressive symptoms (lower is better)

## Study A
Found: harm
Claim: In PD patients given vitamin D3, folic acid and B12 for 6 months, the 15D depression dimension score significantly increased (improved) from baseline.
Sentence: "After the intervention, the mean score of speech, mental function, discomfort and symptoms, depression, and QoL significantly increased (p < 0.05 for all)."
Measured as: depression (15D dimension score)
Population: Levodopa-treated Parkinson's disease patients in Romania, mean age 71 years
Intervention: Daily tablet with 800 IU vitamin D3, 1000 µg folic acid, 15 µg vitamin B12 for 6 months
Comparator: None (single-arm, baseline vs 6 months)
Design: case series
Sample size: not reported
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported

## Study B
Found: benefit
Claim: Depressive symptom severity on the MADRS fell significantly from baseline to 12 weeks after a multicomponent personalized dietary program that included vitamin D3 supplementation.
Sentence: "At the endpoint, a significant reduction in depressive symptom severity was observed on the MADRS (from 15.52 ± 12.01 to 13.20 ± 11.66 points; p < 0.001) and HADS (from 17.00 ± 7.58 to 14.88 ± 7.82 points; p = 0.004)."
Measured as: depressive symptom severity (MADRS)
Population: 25 female patients with bipolar disorder or recurrent depression, mean age 31.3 years
Intervention: 12-week personalized dietary modification and nutrition education with targeted supplementation of omega-3, vitamin D3, magnesium and sodium butyrate
Comparator: none (single-arm, before vs after)
Design: case series
Sample size: 25
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported

content.text: {"rationale":"Study A's 15D depression dimension rose, which is an improvement, yet it is labelled harm; with no comparator and no depression-specific scale, this pair does not show vitamin D results that truly conflict.","verdict":"apparent","reason":"outcome_measure","also_differs":["population","intervention"],"detail":"15D single depression dimension (QoL instrument, higher = better) vs MADRS depression severity (lower = better); both single-arm with no control, so neither isolates vitamin D"}
